Data Center Permitting & Enforcement
We’ve heard via Governor Abbott”s executive order that all new data
centers will be audited by the Public Utilities Commission of Texas with
respect to their impact on the electrical grid, water usage and quality of life
for nearby neighborhoods, prior to permits being issued. I have inquired,
but not yet heard what parameters will be measured with respect to
minimum setbacks from private property, noise levels, vibrations, and air
quality. Do we know what are healthy levels regarding these things? Will
there be before-and-after measurements to insure compliance? And how
will the requirements be enforced during implementation?

It would seem that data centers and their attendant noise and pollution
should be required to be located at least 1/2 mile from residential
neighborhoods, perhaps further for larger facilities.

Hopefully, reasonable and responsible data center regulations will be
developed, written and enforced in order to preserve nearby
neighborhoods’ quality of life and property values. In the meantime please
restrict new data center permitting until these issues are resolved.

Robert McLeod
521 Llano Court
Keller, TX 76248
